item.title: He Recorded the Police. So the Police Apparently Decided to Record His Entire Fucking Life.
item.description:
Napoleon Jones, a Navy veteran, did something dangerously radical in Wisconsin: he stood at a safe distance and lawfully recorded a traffic stop. According to his federal lawsuit, he was subsequently stopped and arrested, spent five hours in custody, and walked out with no citation and no criminal charge. An internal memo reviewed by Reason reportedly says the deputy's supervisor concluded the stop itself had been illegal. Jones filed a complaint. And then things get fucking Orwellian. His lawyer later discovered that deputies had reportedly searched Flock's automated license-plate-reader network for Jones' white BMW more than 100 times in the weeks after the incident. Some searches were allegedly performed by the same deputy involved in his arrest. Jones wasn't accused of another crime; his amended lawsuit alleges the searches lacked a legitimate law-enforcement purpose and were retaliation for exercising his First Amendment rights. That's the nightmare with mass surveillance infrastructure: we're always promised it's there to find dangerous people. Then somebody pisses off the wrong person with access to the database and suddenly it's: "Enhance... enhance... enhance... where did the guy who complained about me go for groceries Tuesday?" And this isn't occurring in a vacuum. Wisconsin authorities are already tightening restrictions around Flock amid other documented cases of officers allegedly or criminally misusing the system for personal surveillance. Technology doesn't magically remove abuse of authority. Sometimes it just gives abuse of authority a search bar. And perhaps the most absurd part? The citizen was recording the police because he wanted accountability. The alleged response was to use a surveillance network to watch him. That's not irony anymore. That's fucking product integration. ♂️ https://reason.com/2026/09/02/wisconsin-cops-used-flock-over-100-times-to-track-a-navy-veteran-after-he-lawfully-recorded-a-traffic-stop/

item.title: GovBrief Today #580
item.description: Donald Trump's Justice Department told the states to turn in their immigrants or their neediest families will lose their welfare checks. Every state shares $16.4 billion in cash aid for needy families. For 28 years only welfare offices had to report undocumented immigrants to Washington. Now every state agency must, including the DMV and the board that licenses people who cut hair. The government said the change "does not impose new obligations on states," then added that they can always give up the money. Every mob movie has the scene where the man in the doorway is sorry to bother you and would hate to see anything happen to the store. This time the people who get hurt are the families who need help the most. I've emailed 8,935 stories over 580 straight nights, free and without ads. The algorithm can't show them all to you.
